newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 15.

text.p: THE DOMINION

McKinnon tries to mend Iran rift: Emergency talks between the government and the Iranian ambassador on Monday night may have averted a diplomatic rift that threatened the multi-million-dollar trade between the two countries. Page 1.

Maori agency 'breached agreement with government': Maori broadcasting agency Te Mangai Paho committed a "serious breach" of its agreement with the government by not alerting it to concerns about Aotearoa Television Network. Page 1.

MPs' thumbs-down for museum logo: The Museum of New Zealand's new name and logo -- a stylised thumbprint symbol -- has been given the thumbs-down by some MPs including Cultural Affairs Minister Christine Fletcher. Page 2.

NZ to fight apple ban: International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith will contest the Australian decision to continue a ban on importing New Zealand apples when he meets his Australian counterpart, Tim Fischer, on Wednesday. Page 2.
'Gatekeepers' to vet NZ$94m building plan: A controversial $94 million new ministerial building is to be scrutinised by "gatekeeping" ministers as part of the budget round. Page 2.
Contest poll, MP tells Latimer: Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare challenged Maori Council chairman Sir Graham Latimer on Monday to put his popularity to the test at the next election. Page 2.

Commerce Commission rejects deal: Goodman Fielder is not yet giving up on its bid to buy the milling and baking assets of Chrischurch-based Defiance Food Industries, despite the Commerce Commission's rejection of the deal on Monday. Page 11.

February result gives Kirks confidence: Wellington department store Kirkcaldie and Stains, reporting a profit of $1.236 million for the six months to February 28, is confident it will beat last year's record full-year result. Page 11.
Waltus seeks $21.7m for shopping centre: Waltus Group wants to raise $21.78 million to build a $42 million shopping centre in Albany in a joint venture with developr Challenge Properties. Page 11.

Dealers comfortable with Skellerup debt: Institutional bond dealers said on Monday they remained comfortable with their holdings of Skellerup Finance debt and rumours of difficult trading for its Levene subsidiary were neither new nor unexpected. Page 11.
CHHP buys Australian plastics firm: Carter Holt Harvey Packaging has bought Australian plastics firm Associated Plastics Industries for an undisclosed sum. Page 11.
Telecom shares 'only moderately undervalued': International finance house Morgan Stanley says Telecom shares are only moderately undervalued. Page 11.
Companies Act still to come for ATN: Aotearoa Television Network's board of directors and executives may soon find themselves facing the rigours of the 1993 Companies Act. Page 12.

Developer pulls out of Opua marina plan after dispute: Maina developer Hopper Developments has pulled out of a $20 million project at Opua, Northland, that had been expected to create up to 100 new jobs. Page 12.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Govt clings to hope on Iranian trade: The government late on Monday night clung to hope that trade with Iran would continue despite an earlier statement from the Iranian Embassy that it had been suspended "until further notice."
Families end December 3.5pc richer in assets: New Zealand households ended the last December quarter 3.5 percent richer than they began it, according to the Westpac FPG household savings indicators.

New TV4 promises bargain rates for adverts: The media industry is bracing itself for yet another advertising war, following the launch of TV3's new channel in Auckland on Monday evening. The new channel, which will be known simply as TV4, is promising bargain rates for advertisers.

Phillips regarded Pacer as personal cashbox -- lawyer: The trial of the former Pacer Kerridge Corporation executive chairman, David Phillips, on fraud charges involving $15.1 million began in the High Court at Auckland on Monday, 16 months after his committal for trial and a decade after the offences
were allegedly committed.
THE PRESS

Weyerhaeuser keen of processing: United States forestry giant Weyerhaeuser is to continue persuing Fletcher Challenge Forests' plans to establish a wood-processing facility in the Wai-iti Valley, says Weyerhaeuser director of finance and planning for timberlands operations, Steve Rosselli. Page 16.

TasAg cops flak over proposed archive sale: Dunedin politician Michael Cullen, a former historian, says he is "disappointed" local company Tasman Agriculture is preparing to sell 5.5 tonnes of historic documents from the Tasmanian State
Archive. Page 16.

Aakland stake: Jim Scott, former chief executive of Air NZ, has bought a controlling stake in the Christchurch firm, Aakland Chemicals, and will run it in a joint venture with three senior staff as minority shareholders. Page 16.
